image_description: A close-up view of a large whale's head emerging vertically from deep blue water. The rostrum is arched and covered in mottled grey skin with distinct white patches (barnacles/callosities). The mouth appears slightly open or the jaw structure is visible, showing the characteristic shape of a baleen whale. Water splashes around the base of the emergence.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly shows the arched rostrum typical of a grey whale. While the blowholes are at the very top edge and partially obscured by the angle/splash, the overall head shape and arch are consistent with the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture is highly detailed, showing the characteristic mottling and white callosities/barnacle patches associated with grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a tight crop focused solely on the head and anterior body. The posterior back where dorsal knuckles would be located is completely outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the head and neck region are visible. The full spindle-shaped body cannot be verified due to cropping and submersion.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the head checkpoints, the visible skin exhibits the correct mottled pattern and barnacle coverage.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is not sufficiently open or angled to reveal the internal baleen plates. They are occluded by the jaw/rostrum structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The pectoral fins are submerged and outside the visible frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is completely outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The high-resolution texture on the head confirms the rough, callosity-covered skin typical of the species.
